document.title: Mahmud on Failed Kandahar Trip (Islamabad 05452)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Confidential] Mahmoud's September 28 two-hour meeting with Taliban Deputy Foreign Minister Jalil ends with no progress; Mullah Omar agreed only to 'think about' proposals. The Ambassador confirms the U.S. will not negotiate with the Taliban.

persons.name: Ahmed Mahmud
persons.role: Director General of Pakistan's ISI (ISID) who travelled to Kandahar in September 2001

mentions.quote: Director of ISID General Ahmed Mahmud provided Ambassador ... read out of his unsuccessful September trip to Kandahar.
Mahmud left them alone to talk while he met separately with Taliban cabinet members led by Deputy Foreign Minister Jalil.

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Taliban leader, met Pakistani religious leaders in Kandahar

mentions.quote: persuading Mullah omar to resolve the fate of terrorist Usama bin Laden
Omar rejected the proposal because he believed they would be biased

persons.name: Usama bin Laden
persons.role: Terrorist leader sheltered in Afghanistan; subject of Pakistani effort to secure his expulsion

mentions.quote: Mahmud asked them to persuade Omar to expel UBL so that 'the barrel of the gun would shift away from Afghanistan.'

persons.name: Abdul Jalil
persons.role: Taliban Deputy Foreign Minister; led Taliban cabinet members meeting Mahmud

mentions.quote: His two-hour meeting with Taliban Deputy Foreign Minister Jalil concluded with no progress.
Jalil said the Taliban would not deport the detainees before the conclusion of the trial.
Jalil contradicted previous assurances by Taliban Ambassador to Pakistan Zaeef that the SNI detainees would be released shortly.

persons.name: Wendy Chamberlin
persons.role: US Ambassador to Pakistan; received Mahmud's readout

mentions.quote: Ambassador confirmed that the United States would not negotiate with the Taliban

persons.name: Altif Ali Khan
persons.role: Lawyer for the Shelter Now detainees; arrived in Kabul 28 Sep 2001

mentions.quote: Their lawyer, Altif Ali Khan, arrived in Kabul Friday evening, September 28.

persons.name: George W. Bush
persons.role: US President, stated there would be no negotiations

mentions.quote: He said President Bush had been quite clear in asserting there would be no negotiations.

events.description: Mahmud travelled to Kandahar, met Taliban Deputy FM Jalil for two hours seeking release of eight Shelter Now detainees; no progress.
Eight Pakistani religious leaders introduced to Mullah Omar by Mahmud; Omar rejected international delegation proposal and would only 'think about' vetting.
Lawyer Altif Ali Khan arrived in Kabul for the detainees.
Shelter Now detainees' trial expected to resume.
Cable Islamabad 5452 sent reporting Mahmud's readout.
Mahmud's trip to Kandahar to seek release of Shelter Now detainees and to bring Pakistani religious leaders to meet Mullah Omar over bin Laden; failed.
Two-hour meeting between Mahmud and Deputy Foreign Minister Jalil on the Shelter Now detainees; no progress.
Eight Pakistani religious leaders meet Mullah Omar; Omar rejects international delegation proposal but will 'think about' vetted version.
Lawyer Altif Ali Khan arrived in Kabul to represent the SNI detainees.
Trial of the eight Shelter Now detainees expected to resume, lasting two or three days.
Embassy Islamabad cable 05452 reports Mahmud's readout to Washington.

key_claims: ISI chief Mahmud's Kandahar mission aimed at releasing eight Shelter Now detainees and persuading Omar to expel Usama bin Laden.
Taliban Deputy FM Jalil refused to deport detainees before the trial's conclusion.
Mullah Omar rejected an international clerical delegation but agreed only to 'think about' Pakistani vetting.
Pakistani religious leaders with ties to former students among the Taliban were used as intermediaries.
Mahmud feared fallout among radical elements in Pakistan from US military action.
The US told Mahmud it would not negotiate with the Taliban and was on a fast track.
